title: Ronwen Williams insists Bafana Bafana have learnt from 2012 Afcon 'Dance of Shame' ahead of Kenya clashes
text:

 Sign In SPORT Ronwen Williams insists Bafana Bafana have learnt from 2012 Afcon 'Dance of Shame' ahead of Kenya clashes
 Africa Cup of Nations 2027 qualifiers
 Video Mihlali Baleka 
 13 NOV 2026, 08:20 3 min read Bafana Bafana captain Ronwen Williams has urged his teammates to push for maximum points against Kenya to avoid a repeat of their 2012 Afcon qualification heartbreak. | Backpagepix Picture: Backpagepix Incidents like the infamous “Dance of Shame” of the Africa Cup of Nations 2012 qualifiers still live fresh in the memory of Bafana Bafana captain Ronwen Williams , who revealed why they have been forced to leave no stone unturned in Group D of the ongoing qualifiers. 
 Bafana are in a group that includes co-hosts Kenya, who they face on Friday (kick-off 6pm). As such, the qualification dynamics carry unique stakes: only one non-host nation from the group – between South Africa, Guinea, and Eritrea – can punch a ticket to the tournament. 
 That nation must either win the group outright or finish as runners-up behind the Harambee Stars come the end of the campaign in March next year, after the penultimate and final rounds of qualifiers. 
 Bafana were victims of failing to understand the rules 14-years ago. They drew 0-0 with Sierra Leone in the last qualifier, thinking that they had qualified for the finals via the goal difference rule, whereas the group standings – in the event of a points tie – were decided on head-to-head results. 
 That result still haunts Bafana, especially after the likes of Itumeleng Khune, Siphiwe Tshabalala, and Andile Jali led the team in a jubilant dance, which has been dubbed the “Dance of Shame”. 
 Ironically, Bafana coach Pitso Mosimane , who was the tactician at the time, has ensured – together with Williams – that the players are aware of the dynamics that come with having the Harambee Stars in their group. 
 “Yes, definitely. Most players, and everyone knows. The coach has made mention of it, ” Williams said. 
 “We’ve had our history where we didn’t know the rules, or something like that. We don’t want to put ourselves in that situation again. 
 “We know that we have Kenya in our group, so come the last two games in March, everyone is going to go for it, but the main one is now. If we get six points now, you guys (the media) can start packing your bags already. We’d have one foot in. ” 
 Crucially, Bafana need the six points during this window against the same Kenya side, who’ll visit them at Orlando Amstel Arena on Friday night (6pm) before the return leg is played in Nairobi on Tuesday. 
 Given all that, Williams is pleased with the start to the qualifiers that saw them top the group with a maximum six points from two matches, but has called for his teammates to put in an extra shift in the next two games. 
 “We are excited that we started [well], we now need to just maintain it. Can we be better (than the last games)? The coach has asked us just to even be 5% better as a team; that will show that we are on the right track, and there’s room for improvement, ” Williams said. 
 “Even the last camp was amazing, we bagged three wonderful victories. But the coach is asking for more. It’s scary what this team can do in the next few months, starting (tonight). ”  |  IOL Sport
